findings.body: Both attempts authenticate because validation only checks membership and never removes the matched code, so the new integration test does not exercise the one-time-use recovery-code behavior.
findings.failure_mode: The test user-storage implementation models recovery codes as reusable passwords rather than consumable codes.
findings.impact: Both attempts authenticate because validation only checks membership and never removes the matched code, so the new integration test does not exercise the one-time-use recovery-code behavior.
findings.root_cause: Recovery-code validation was implemented as a read-only membership check.
findings.suggested_fix: On a successful match, remove the matched code from the persisted recovery-code list before returning true, and add a test that verifies replay is rejected.
findings.title: The recovery-code test provider accepts the same recovery code indefinitely

findings.verifier_reason: Line 340 exists verbatim. The validation uses anyMatch() which only checks membership without removing the matched code. Real RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid() calls removeRecoveryAuthnCode() after successful validation. This test provider allows unlimited reuse of recovery codes, failing to test one-time-use semantics.

raw_findings.body: The recovery credential remains in the user-storage provider because the existing recovery credential provider deletes via removeStoredCredentialById, which only addresses local storage; the supposedly removed recovery codes can remain configured and usable.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Credential deletion only targets the local store while the active credential resides in user storage.
raw_findings.impact: The recovery credential remains in the user-storage provider because the existing recovery credential provider deletes via removeStoredCredentialById, which only addresses local storage; the supposedly removed recovery codes can remain configured and usable.
raw_findings.root_cause: Recovery codes are newly persisted through the federated update API without adding a corresponding federated removal lifecycle.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a federated-credential deletion path for recovery codes (or route deletion to the owning user-storage updater) and use it whenever creation succeeded in user storage.
raw_findings.title: Federated recovery credentials cannot be removed through the existing credential lifecycle

finding.trigger: A federated user-storage provider accepts this update, and the user later removes the recovery-code credential through account/admin credential management.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that federated recovery credentials cannot be removed is speculative. The patch adds creation support via updateCredential(), and the existing disableCredentialType() method in UserCredentialManager already delegates to user storage providers. No evidence shows the deletion path is broken - removeStoredCredentialById targets local storage by design, while federated providers handle their own credential lifecycle through disableCredentialType().
